text:
micah: quick async update from me — landed the microkernel change that tweaks the queueing fairness (packet->slot rebalancer). ran a focused local run: tail latency improved a lot on our synthetic chat workload. CI is flaky so holding off on rollout until infra check. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 :eyes:

anya: wow nice. can you drop the perf snapshot here? numbers + test config pls. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

micah: sure — short numbers from my local perf harness (A100-like host, seq=512, 4x clients): p50 ~ -20%, p95 ~ -35%, p99 ~ -48% vs main, throughput roughly flat. raw logs + config: https://gist.github.com/micah/perf-1788

ravi: can we gate this behind a runtime feature flag? worried about interaction with KV warmup path — saw OOM-ish traces on small nodes during earlier prefetch experiments.

micah: added a boolean flag in the PR (default off). pushed the patch to flip default once canary is green. snippet: ```yaml
runtime:
  features:
    amphora_queue_rebalance: false
```

ravi: thanks. FYI the eviction thrash looked like concurrent prefetch + aggressive fill. temp mitigation: reduce prefetch parallelism to 4 in the warmup controller until we have a proper backpressure hook.

jade: I can run the canary on Dedicated pool-3 at 10:30 PT and watch for evictions + swap. tagging ops-bot to schedule. :clock10:

ops-bot: Deploy job scheduled by jade for pool-3 @ 2026-03-17T10:30:00-07:00 — canary rollout will target 3 nodes, monitor window 20m. (job id: deploy-2026-1788-amphora)

ravi: pinging @sre-oncall — we saw a few swap/oom alerts last night that may be related to the warmup behavior. can you keep an eye on node mem pressure during the canary?

sre-oncall: saw the spike, raised oom_kill_threshold on the affected cluster and cleared noise. will watch the canary window and report if anything looks off.

anya: quick code-review note: left a tiny nit on the PR regarding the metrics tag naming (used "amphora" in one place, "amphora_queue" elsewhere). also asked for a short comment explaining the fairness heuristic. otherwise looks good.

micah: thanks — I'll address the nit and add a test that toggles the feature flag. current blocker for me: flaky integ test `chat_stream_smoke` in CI that times out intermittently. disabling that job for the moment so CI can converge, but we need to re-enable and root cause.

ravi: I can dig into that job later today, looks like a network proxy hang in the job logs. will post findings.

micah: appreciated. plan: fix nits + re-run CI, then small canary per jade's schedule. folks watching canary pls look at latency p99, eviction rate, and per-node memory delta. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood-inference/internal/amphora/canary-1788

jade: I'll watch and post brief notes in this thread after the 20m window. if anything critical happens I'll ping #incidents. :white_check_mark:

micah: sweet — nothing else from me. if anyone has spare cycles before the canary, extra eyes on the CI logs would be huge. thanks! :coffee:
